html.xpu:
Installing on Intel GPU (XPU) Platform

XPU device backend brings native Intel GPU support to PyTorch, enabling performant training and inference on both Linux and Windows.

Prerequisites

The system with configured Intel GPU card is required. For detailed list of supported devices and driver install instructions refer to Getting Started on Intel GPU.

Installation

pip

Use the pip package manager to install PyTorch with XPU support. Select your preferred options in the selector above to get the installation command.

Verification

To ensure that PyTorch was installed correctly with XPU support, run the following code:

import torch
print(torch.__version__)

# Check XPU availability
if torch.xpu.is_available():
    print("XPU is available!")
    print(f"XPU devices: {torch.xpu.device_count()}")
else:
    print("XPU is not available.")

The following, or a similar output, indicates successful installation:

2.13.0+xpu
XPU is available!
XPU devices: 4

Documentation

For more information, please visit the torch.xpu.
html.ascend_npu:
Installing on Ascend NPU

Ascend for PyTorch (TorchNPU) is a deep learning adaptation framework built on Ascend. It enables Ascend NPUs to support the PyTorch framework, delivering the powerful computing capabilities of Ascend AI processors to PyTorch developers and users.

Prerequisites

Hardware Requirements

  • Ascend for PyTorch supports most Ascend platforms. Please check the hardware compatibility before installing.

Software Requirements

  • Python >= 3.10
  • CANN (Compute Architecture for Neural Networks) toolkit installed >= 8.0
  • Ascend driver and firmware installed

Before installing PyTorch with Ascend NPU support, you must install the CANN toolkit. Download it from the Ascend Community and follow the CANN Installation Guide.

Installation

pip

pip3 install torch==2.10.0 --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu && pip3 install torch-npu==2.10.0

Use the pip package manager to install PyTorch with Ascend NPU support. Please refer to the installation page and select your preferred options in the selector above to get the installation command.

Verification

To ensure that PyTorch was installed correctly with Ascend NPU support, run the following code:

import torch
import torch_npu

x = torch.randn(2, 2, device="npu")
y = torch.randn(2, 2, device="npu")
z = x.mm(y)

print(z)

The following, or a similar output, indicates successful installation:

tensor([[-0.0515,  0.3664],
        [-0.1258, -0.5425]],  device='npu:0')

Documentation

For more information, please visit:

  • Ascend for PyTorch Official Documentation (English, Chinese)
  • Ascend Community Portal (English, Chinese)
  • CANN Main Page (English, Chinese)
  • PyTorch Adaptation for Ascend Portal (English, Chinese)
  • Ascend Hardware Compatibility (English coming soon, Chinese)

html.cuda_woa:
Installing on CUDA - Windows on Arm

CUDA - Windows on Arm provides native Windows ARM64 PyTorch, TorchVision and TorchAudio wheels with NVIDIA CUDA support. It uses PyTorch's official in-tree CUDA backend and existing CUDA dispatch keys (it does not introduce a new PrivateUse1 backend), so existing CUDA code runs unchanged on Windows on Arm systems with NVIDIA GPUs. NVIDIA builds pinned upstream PyTorch commits natively for ARM64, publishes stable and nightly packages, and runs the upstream CUDA test suite on self-hosted Windows ARM64 systems. Results are reported to the PyTorch HUD.

Prerequisites

Hardware Requirements

  • A Windows on Arm system with a supported NVIDIA GPU.
  • Supported GPUs
    • NVIDIA RTX Spark

Software Requirements

  • Windows 11 on Arm, 24H2 or later
  • NVIDIA Windows driver R615 or later
  • CUDA 13.4 and cuDNN 9.26 runtime libraries (the CUDA 13.4 wheels are built against these versions)

Installation

pip

python -m pip install "torch==2.14.0+cu134" "torchvision==0.29.0+cu134" "torchaudio==2.11.0+cu134" --extra-index-url https://pypi.nvidia.com/nvtorch_oot/

Use the pip package manager to install PyTorch, TorchVision and TorchAudio with CUDA support from the NVIDIA package index. Select your preferred options in the selector above to get the installation command. Nightly builds are available from https://pypi.nvidia.com/nvtorch_oot_nightly/.

Verification

To ensure that PyTorch was installed correctly with CUDA support, run the following code:

import torch
print(torch.__version__)

# Check CUDA availability
if torch.cuda.is_available():
    print("CUDA is available!")
    print(f"CUDA devices: {torch.cuda.device_count()}")
    print(f"Device name: {torch.cuda.get_device_name(0)}")

    x = torch.randn(2, 2, device="cuda")
    y = torch.randn(2, 2, device="cuda")
    print(x.mm(y))
else:
    print("CUDA is not available.")

The following, or a similar output, indicates successful installation:

2.14.0+cu134
CUDA is available!
CUDA devices: 1
Device name: NVIDIA ...
tensor([[-0.4218,  0.8912],
        [ 0.1534, -1.1045]], device='cuda:0')

Support

  • PyTorch issues: please file them at pytorch/pytorch with the module: cuda-windows-arm64 label.
  • Packaging, build and CI issues: NVIDIA/pytorch-windows-ci.

Documentation

For more information, please visit:

  • Install built wheels
  • Build PyTorch on Windows ARM64
  • Windows on Arm CI coverage
  • CI results on the PyTorch HUD
  • GitHub Repository
html.torch_tpu:
Installing on Google Cloud TPU (TorchTPU)

TorchTPU (torch_tpu) is a native PyTorch backend built for Google Cloud Tensor Processing Units (TPUs). It enables Google Cloud TPUs to run PyTorch workloads natively by integrating as a PrivateUse1 backend using the dispatch key "tpu". TorchTPU supports eager execution, torch.compile(), distributed training (torch.distributed, DTensor, FSDP2), and custom kernels (Pallas, Helion).

Prerequisites

Hardware Requirements

  • A provisioned Google Cloud TPU VM (TPU v5e, v5p, v6e, or v7x) on Google Compute Engine (GCE), access to Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) cluster, or a TPU runtime in Google Colab.

Software Requirements

  • Linux (Ubuntu 22.04+ recommended)
  • Python >= 3.10
  • libtpu runtime library (automatically installed with torch_tpu)

Installation

pip

pip3 install torch --index-url https://download.pytorch.org/whl/cpu && pip3 install torch_tpu

Use the pip package manager to install the CPU build of PyTorch alongside torch_tpu. Select your preferred options in the selector above to get the installation command.

Verification

To ensure that PyTorch was installed correctly with TorchTPU support, run the following code:

import torch

x = torch.randn(2, 2, device="tpu")
y = torch.randn(2, 2, device="tpu")
z = x.mm(y)

print(z)

The following, or a similar output, indicates successful installation:

tensor([[-0.4218,  0.8912],
        [ 0.1534, -1.1045]], device='tpu:0')

Documentation

For more information, please visit:

  • TorchTPU Official Documentation & User Guide
  • Supported vs. Unsupported Feature Matrix
  • Google Cloud TPU Documentation
  • GitHub Repository
  • PyPI
